findings.finding: The original SQL test claimed cross-company link refusal without constructing a second company or attempting such a link, and did not exercise admin behavior or the full member/outsider write surface.
findings.resolution_evidence: The final SQL suite creates two tenant roots, attempts to attach the second tenant's facility to the first tenant's boundary, confirms the original link remains, proves owner/admin writes, and proves member/outsider insert, update, and delete denial across facilities, reporting boundaries, and boundary-facility links.

findings.finding: POST /workspace initially accepted an additional userId field and returned 201, weakening the fixed request and identity boundary even though the field was ignored.
findings.resolution_evidence: The route now performs an exact key-and-value parse after authentication, returns bounded HTTP 422 for any extra or changed field, and the test expects the ownership override attempt to fail.

findings.finding: Synthetic identity controls remained enabled while an authorized request was pending, allowing an owner response to be rendered after the visible actor had been switched to another tenant.
findings.resolution_evidence: All identity controls are disabled while busy. The final browser flow also clears the displayed record immediately when the actor changes.

findings.finding: The initial development server rejected only NODE_ENV=production. An intermediate repair exposed options that could override a real production runtime and start the server programmatically.
findings.resolution_evidence: The exported factory now reads Bun.env directly and starts only when M54_SYNTHETIC_WORKSPACE equals enabled and NODE_ENV equals development or test. Tests mutate and restore the real environment and prove unset, staging, and production states fail closed.

findings.finding: A workspace creation exception, including a duplicate-key database message, could reach the HTTP response body.
findings.resolution_evidence: Creation failures now return only HTTP 409 and the fixed message Workspace could not be created; the test injects a private database detail and proves it is absent.

findings.finding: A workspace lookup exception was independently reproduced as HTTP 500 with the exact thrown private database detail in the response body.
findings.resolution_evidence: Lookup failures now return only HTTP 503 and the fixed message Workspace is unavailable; the regression test injects a private database detail and proves it is absent.

findings.finding: The milestone record retained pre-repair test counts and described only the earlier production guard.
findings.resolution_evidence: The final record reports database 7/40, API 617/5,311, web 53/185, focused M54 20/73, and the exact two-part startup guard.

database_and_rls_results.engine: PGlite 0.3.16, PostgreSQL-in-WASM, fresh in-memory database per test
database_and_rls_results.rls_metadata: Independent pg_class inspection returned relrowsecurity=true and relforcerowsecurity=true for all six tenant tables.
database_and_rls_results.security_definer_controls: is_company_member, can_manage_company, and create_company_workspace are SECURITY DEFINER, use search_path=neuvetra, pg_temp, revoke PUBLIC execute, and grant execute only to authenticated. Qualified relations and auth.uid-derived identity were inspected.
database_and_rls_results.table_grants: authenticated receives SELECT on all six tables; only facilities, reporting_boundaries, and boundary_facilities receive INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. Companies, memberships, and audit events have no authenticated write grant.
database_and_rls_results.identity: The harness sets request.jwt.claim.sub transaction-locally, auth.uid() resolves it, and application methods always set the authenticated role before tenant SQL.
database_and_rls_results.atomic_bootstrap: create_company_workspace executes company, owner membership, facility, reporting boundary, link, and audit inserts in one database function call. A duplicate fixed company is rejected and the first complete workspace remains readable.
database_and_rls_results.role_behavior: Owner and admin can mutate the three supported child-table write surfaces; member can read but cannot mutate; outsider sees zero rows and cannot insert, update, delete, or cross-link.
database_and_rls_results.cross_company_integrity: Composite foreign keys bind boundary_id and facility_id to the same company_id. The final executable test creates a second tenant and rejects a real mixed-company link.

api_and_browser_contract_results.post_origin: An untrusted or absent POST Origin is rejected before authentication and storage access.
api_and_browser_contract_results.get_origin: An explicit foreign GET Origin is rejected; an Origin-less authenticated same-origin browser read through the local proxy is accepted.
api_and_browser_contract_results.authentication: Missing and invalid fixed synthetic bearer tokens return HTTP 401. The request body cannot select a user or tenant.
api_and_browser_contract_results.request_shape: Only the seven fixed synthetic input fields and values are accepted; an added userId is HTTP 422.
api_and_browser_contract_results.inference_boundary: Unknown and foreign valid workspace identifiers return the same HTTP 404 body: Workspace not found.
api_and_browser_contract_results.error_sanitization: Injected create and read store exceptions return bounded 409/503 responses without the thrown database detail.
api_and_browser_contract_results.decoder: The browser accepts only the exact fixed company, geography, facility, eGRID subregion, reporting year, boundary approach/status/version, UUID shapes, and exact object keys.
api_and_browser_contract_results.startup_guard: The loopback server requires both an explicit M54 enable flag and an explicit development/test runtime; it fails closed for unset, staging, and production states.
api_and_browser_contract_results.independent_browser_flow: Through the final loopback API and Vite proxy, the reviewer observed owner creation with Synthetic Acme, Inc., Synthetic California office, US/CA, CAMX, 2023 operational control, draft version 1; owner revisit; Other tenant returning Workspace not found; signed out returning Authentication required; and record clearing on actor change.
api_and_browser_contract_results.accessibility: The rendered demo exposes a level-one heading, a named synthetic-identity group, labeled actor controls, buttons with disabled states, and a polite live status region.
api_and_browser_contract_results.production_bundle_exclusion: A fresh production build completed. Eight M54 markers were absent from dist: both synthetic tokens, both fixture names, /workspace-api, the workspace heading, CompanyWorkspaceDemo, and synthetic-m54.

limitations: PGlite is PostgreSQL-compatible test evidence, not proof that the migration, ownership, auth schema references, RLS policies, or grants behave identically in the hosted Supabase project. No hosted migration was run.

Authentication uses two fixed non-secret synthetic tokens and a transaction-local auth.uid simulation. No real JWT, Supabase session, OTP, token expiry, refresh, or authenticator/anon role path was tested.
Storage is memory-only and is lost when the process stops. No persistence, backup, restore, rollback, schema-upgrade, or concurrent multi-process behavior was tested.

M54 establishes only the relational tenant root. Bill files, parsers, object storage, search, background jobs, caches, logs, calculation persistence, retention, and deletion are absent and therefore receive no isolation acceptance.

The audit event is immutable to the authenticated application role in this schema, but privileged database operators remain outside this bounded test and no production audit-retention control was reviewed.
No customer data, secrets, external network, production system, qualified penetration test, or human legal/accounting/assurance review was involved.
The repository was dirty. Any change to a reviewed file invalidates this byte-bound review until the changed hash and affected behavior are reviewed again.
